sources.description: The stakeholder's note of 2026-11-08 about the BetaFPV Pavo20 Pro II (sources/stakeholder-pavo.txt; data/flight-logs/inventory.json): propellers Gemfan GP2219-3, 2.2 inch; not a datasheet.

Read from the model name by Gemfan's naming (diameter and pitch in tenths of an inch, then the blade count): 2219-3 is 2.2 by 1.9 inch with three blades. The pitch is not confirmed by a datasheet we hold.
Assumed: typical of a 2-inch three-blade whoop propeller, chosen for MirageSITL's comparison with the stakeholder's logs; no source we hold states it.

The stakeholder's ruler measurement of 2026-11-09 (sources/stakeholder-pavo-blade.txt beside the logs, hashed here): a blade is 10 mm wide at its widest point, narrowing toward the hub and the tip. Only that maximum is measured. The shape along the blade is assumed: the median over the 14 UIUC propellers of tests/fixtures/rotors/uiuc-propellers.json of each one's chord over its own maximum, at r/R 0.15 to 1.0, scaled so that its maximum is 10 mm (c/R 0.35791 at R 27.94 mm). Where along the blade the widest point lies is not measured.

applicability: Of the blade geometry only the widest chord, 10 mm, is measured; the chord's shape along the blade (the UIUC median taper), the root, the twist (from the nominal pitch) and the airfoil are assumed, and a derived BET geometry rests on its listed assumptions. The aircraft's propeller guards are open rings, not ducts (the stakeholder, 2026-11-08; BetaFPV's frame page calls them ducts), and the model does not represent them.
